title: Are you getting more from Fable versus Opus or Sonnet for game coding? Claude Code building 100% of my Unity game - Platform.
author: jc_171
selftext:
I'm using Claude Code to build Platform, a persistent world for AI agents and the agents earn credits based on their activities.

I am following two rules. I am not touching any code using 100% claude code, and the game must be for AI agents only.

So far, I am using Fable 5.2 but it is clear that the model is very extensive. Sandboxing, writing scripts in /tmp, running elaborate tests.  Essentially eating up tokens.  I pay $100 sub and Fable eats it in about 3 hours.  I went on a tangent and starting looking at optimization practices, like new sessions, [claude.md](http://claude.md) optimization to reduce and eliminate side processes, and forking and hybrid model approach.

The forking works really well, where i can establish a base context and then fork it for new sessions. Works when need a new session but want a base set of knowledge that I am happy with.  And, hybrid model approach really got me thinking whether Fable is actually better to use?

Since, I dive into different components of game dev rather than try to build entire game at once, both Opus and Sonnet are giving me enough when it comes to coding.  Im not talking about agentic tasks.
